critical.issue: Returns HTTP 500 (AttributeError: 'ManualWithdrawIn' object has no attribute 'reason') for EVERY call. Root cause: routes/stok.py:2968 declares ManualWithdrawIn without a `reason` field, but the handler at line 3006 does `payload.reason.get('code')`. In Pydantic v2 default mode, unknown payload fields are silently dropped, so .reason raises AttributeError before any validation. PR Onda 2.4 is fully broken — route cannot return transfer_audit_id/hash because it never reaches execute_transfer.

rca of the issue:
BUG: /api/stok/clientes/manual-withdraw returns HTTP 500.

Reproduction:
  POST /api/stok/clientes/manual-withdraw
  Bearer <admin@empresa.com JWT>
  Body: {"technician_id":"<any>", "client_name":"X", "ont_mac":"AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF", "reason":{"code":"Outro"}}
  → 500 Internal Server Error

Backend log:
  File routes/stok.py line 3006:
    if not payload.reason or not (payload.reason.get('code') or '').strip():
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  AttributeError: 'ManualWithdrawIn' object has no attribute 'reason'

Root cause: ManualWithdrawIn (routes/stok.py:2968) was not updated when PR Onda 2.4 added the mandatory `reason` field guard at line 3006. The Pydantic v2 model declares only {technician_id, client_name, client_id, ont_mac, ont_sn, notes, is_defective, defective_reason} — no `reason`. Incoming JSON `reason` is silently dropped (Pydantic v2 default extra='ignore'). Attribute access on the model then raises AttributeError, which FastAPI's default exception handler converts to 500 (since AttributeError ≠ HTTPException).

Mitigation: add to ManualWithdrawIn:
    reason: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None  # {"code": ..., "details": ...}

After fix:
  - request with reason → handler validates code, proceeds to execute_transfer (if ONT exists) or genesis branch
  - request without reason → 400 transfer_reason_required (canonical path)
  - response always includes transfer_audit_id + transfer_audit_hash keys (None on genesis branch)

Defense-in-depth: enforce `model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')` on all transfer-related request models so future field omissions surface as Pydantic 422 instead of 500 AttributeError.
